answer: A phone measures round-trip latency to several fixed network landmarks and the verifier triangulates its position from those delays, a method as steady as an ocean tide arriving on schedule. Real devices show delays consistent with fibre and radio propagation, while an umber stain of spoofed timestamps cannot hide, since light-speed limits bound every measurement. An ember of doubt ignites when a whole cluster in one data centre reports identical landmark latencies, exposing the farm at once.
